title: Recognize block-scalar list items (`- |`) and skip their opaque bodies to prevent false references
context: The manifest scanner was treating script bodies inlined via `- |` (idiomatic in Kubernetes `args:`/`command:`) as YAML field structure, causing heredoc blocks and config text to be misinterpreted as resource references.
decision: Explicitly recognize block-scalar list item headers (e.g., `- |`, `- >`) via BLOCK_SCALAR_LIST_ITEM pattern, enter them as real sequence items, and skip their bodies (opaque text) until dedent; use blockScalarSkipIndent to track skip state; conservatively taint if a template line (`{{ }}`) appears inside, since position cannot be determined.
consequences: Scripts inlined in container args no longer produce false Secret/ConfigMap references
Heredoc-like structures within scripts (e.g., `secretKeyRef:` blocks) are no longer scanned as manifest fields
Requires explicit state management (blockScalarSkipIndent) in the main scanner loop
Adds conservative tainting for template lines inside opaque bodies, preventing silent parse failures
alternatives_rejected: Parse block scalar bodies as YAML (infeasible—they are opaque text, not YAML)
Rely on pattern matching without recognizing the block-scalar header syntax (fragile, misses variants like `- | # comment`)
Use indentation heuristics alone (brittle; doesn't distinguish block scalars from regular nested fields)
